title: client-request-annotary-lab-notes-march-2026
content:
TL;DR:
Small-but-recurrent customer asks around (a) partial KV cache invalidation, (b) shorter cold-start routes for small-batch low-latency, and (c) visibility into per-request model-fallback cause. This doc compiles raw customer snippets, quick frequency tallies from the last 90 days, pragmatic mitigation ideas (low-effort -> medium -> engineering), and a proposed micro-patch plan for next sprint.

Context and why this matters:
- Multiple mid-market customers are bumping into cost/latency tradeoffs when using persistent KV caching with mixed workloads (bursty short chitchat + occasional long context jobs). They prefer deterministic ways to evict or scope caches per-route or per-deployment.
- Hosted API customers want a predictable low-latency route for <8-token responses that bypasses batching heuristics during business hours.
- Several customers surfaced opaque fallbacks (app saw model X, then suddenly model Y returned; no reason surfaced in logs). This increases support load and trust risks.

Raw customer snippets (anonymized):
- "We see 200ms spikes every 30s — seems tied to other tenants' long-context jobs. Can we scope cache or pin model variants for our app?"
- "Is there a quick knob to flush the KV for one deployment? Currently we restart but that's heavy-handed."
- "We get a different model sometimes after retry — we need a reason in the response or a header we can ingest."

Quick tally (last 90 days, derived from CS tickets + Slack tags):
- KV-cache scoping/eviction asks: ~18 distinct accounts; recurring from 6 accounts
- Short-route latency bypass requests (small-batch low-latency): ~12 accounts, peak after marketing product launches
- Model-fallback visibility requests: ~9 accounts (high severity for 3 enterprise deals)
- Workarounds reported: customer restarts, local client-side throttling, duplication of short/long traffic into separate deployments

Impact hypothesis and engineering effort estimate:
- User impact: medium-high (affects SLA-sensitive customers and renewals)
- Engineering rough classes:
  * Low-effort (1–2 dev-days): API flags + response header for fallback reason; admin console toggle to purge cache for a deployment
  * Medium-effort (1–2 sprints): Route-level cache scoping and a per-route sticky KV namespace; short-route bypass path for sub-10-token flows (policy switch)
  * High-effort (multi-sprint): Dynamic cache partitioning + formal resource isolation for mixed long/short workloads across tenants

Proposed micro-patch plan (MVP first):
1) Add a response header X-RW-Fallback-Reason on any request which returned from a fallback path. Include machine-friendly codes: capacity, model-unavailable, region-failover, policy (example: model-unavailable). (Owner: Eng-Observability, Estimate: 2 dev-days)
2) Expose a one-click "Purge KV cache" action in Console per-deployment (admin-only). Backend route calls existing in-memory purger. Log action to audit trail. (Owner: Console + Serving-Runtime, Estimate: 3–4 dev-days)
3) Experimental route flag: "low-latency-passthrough" that disables batching and runs through a fast-path for requests under N tokens. Start gated behind feature flag and only for Hosted customers on Standard/Dedicated. (Owner: Serving Runtime, Estimate: 2 week spike + 1 week rollout)

Operational notes / SLO considerations:
- Purge action should not be allowed during autoscale reconfiguration windows. Add guard and clear UI warning.
- X-RW-Fallback-Reason must be sampled in traces and sent to Tracestore for debug correlation.

Open questions / risks:
- Security: does allowing purge increase risk of accidental data exposure? (Answer: purge only deletes transient KV pointers, not stored user data — need to confirm with infra/security)
- Billing interplay: bypassing batching may increase per-token cost — how are we going to surface cost impact to customers? Suggest adding estimated cost delta in Console when flag enabled.
- Can we implement the low-latency path without regressing throughput for shared nodes? Might require route routing to dedicated micro-pools.

Proposed priority (triage matrix):
- Phase A (next 2 sprints): header + console purge + documentation + customer comms for workaround
- Phase B (Q2): route-level scoping and low-latency passthrough beta for 5 pilot customers
- Phase C (later): partitioned cache and stronger tenancy isolation work

Suggested owners and stakeholders:
- Customer Success: Ava Martinez (owner for customer comms + pilot coordination)
- Eng (Serving Runtime): Priya Singh (technical owner for low-latency path)
- Eng (Console + Observability): Liam Chen (console purge + header + trace mapping)
- Security/Compliance: loop-in for purge semantics and audit trail

Customer-facing messaging draft (short):
"We heard that mixed short/long traffic can cause unpredictable latency. We're rolling out a set of small fixes to give you immediate control (cache purge, per-request visibility) and then a beta for a faster low-latency route. If you'd like to pilot the early beta, reply here and we'll onboard you."

Next steps (who does what this week):
- Ava: prepare a short pilot invite list (target 6 customers) and draft customer email (due: 2026-03-18)
- Priya: spike on low-latency passthrough feasibility, doc findings in GH issue (due: 2026-03-20) -> link to GH issue on doc
- Liam: implement X-RW-Fallback-Reason header + small console control to trigger purge; create demo video for CS (deliverable: 2026-03-25)
- Security: one-off quick review for purge semantics (due: 2026-03-19)

Notes-to-self / friction log (for internal trace):
- Look up past incident where fallback happened silently (search: incident/fallback-march-2025)
- Collect cost delta numbers for passthrough vs normal path (ask FinOps)

Appendix: partial raw ticket excerpts (redacted)
- Ticket #CS-3124: "Model changed mid-flow; logs show fallback due to 'capacity' but no client-facing reason"
- Ticket #CS-3218: "We created a short-only deployment as workaround — awkward to manage and duplicates billing"

End of document.

(If this becomes useful, we should keep a running "annotary" lab notebook for similar small triage+micro-patch threads to show velocity and reduce duplicate asks.)
